headlines.snippet: Natanel Shkaron is the victim of a shooting attack at a spring in Benjamin; the attacker was captured in a hospital in Ramallah. A terrorist opened fire on people at a spring near Neve Tzuf, abandoned his vehicle, and fled on foot. Natanel Shkaron, a father of six from Eli Zehav, who came to immerse himself before Yom Kippur, was evacuated in critical condition to Beilinson Hospital, where his death was pronounced. After an extensive manhunt, Duvdevan unit soldiers apprehended the terrorist in a Ramallah hospital, after he was wounded by IDF tracker fire during the pursuit. About an hour later, a second terrorist attempting a ramming attack in the northern West Bank was neutralized.

headlines.snippet: Yom Kippur 2026 (5787): Times for the start and end of the fast across the country and the world, customs, and laws. The fast of Yom Kippur 5787 will begin this evening with sunset on Sunday, September 20, 2026 (Tishrei 9) and will end after nightfall on Monday, September 21, 2026 (Tishrei 10). The fast begins today in Jerusalem at 17:58, in Tel Aviv at 18:22, and in Haifa at 18:09, with times varying by city. The fast lasts approximately 25 hours, during which eating, drinking, washing, wearing leather shoes, anointing, and marital relations are prohibited.
